title: What is a fixed match?
body_html:
WHAT IS A FIXED MATCH?

Many definitions of so-called fixed matches exist and are in use today. For the purposes of this Guide, however, we will use the definition in the Council of Europe Convention* on the Manipulation of Sports Competitions (also known as the Macolin Convention), as it is the best known and most widely accepted internationally:

*Manipulation of sports competitions means an intentional arrangement, act or omission aimed at an improper alteration of the result or the course of a sports competition in order to remove all or part of the unpredictable nature of that sports competition, with a view to obtaining an undue advantage for oneself or for others.

Cases that fall within this definition include:

• Deliberately losing a match or one of its stages, for whatever reason or purpose;

• A participant’s deliberate underperformance, or a player’s deliberate withdrawal in breach of the rules before the end of the match (also known as “tanking”);

• Micro-manipulation of sporting events — fixing intermediate results of certain elements of a sports competition;

• A referee’s and/or other competition organisers’ deliberately incorrect application of the rules of the game;

• Interfering with the course of play, or damaging the playing surfaces or equipment available to the venue’s staff.

The fraudulent use of inside information* does not always match the definition above, as it does not involve manipulating real events, but it is a way of misleading betting operators by using certain information about a sporting event that is not available to the public.

*Inside information – information relating to any competition that a person possesses by virtue of their position in relation to a sport or competition, excluding information already published or common knowledge, easily accessible to the interested public or disclosed in accordance with the rules and regulations governing the competition concerned.

Consequently, any case giving rise to reasonable suspicion that inside information is being used to place bets on the outcome of a sporting event will be treated as match-fixing fraud.
